rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı frames the challenge as answering doubts about revelation, including whether God sends books, why this one came piecemeal, and whether it is merely human poetry or invention.
rows.anchor: meselâ “vahiy inanılır şey midir? Allah kitap gönderecek olsa böyle mi gönderir? Böyle parça parça,

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge is to produce a surah matching the Qur’an in style, eloquence, and originality; ideally its speaker would be unlettered and morally like Muhammad.
rows.anchor: bir sûre de siz bulunuz ve ona tam benzemek için söyleyen de o kulumuz gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says the challenge even waives the proposed condition that the imitator be unlettered and morally like Muhammad, allowing any person to attempt it.
rows.anchor: Haydi bu son kaydı da hazf edelim, size müsaade eyleyelim, ‘ale’l-ıtlâk her hangi bir şahıstan olursa olsun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invitees include every trusted ally or supposed source of aid: deities, idols, poets, writers, scholars, sages, leaders, and anyone who might support the challengers.
rows.anchor: ne kadar yardımcılarınız, tanıdığınız ne kadar mâbudlarınız, iktidarını farz ettiğiniz ne kadar putlarınız, şuarânız, üdebânız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuhadāʾ is the plural of shahīd, which can mean present, witness, helper, or exemplary model; here it means any such supporter.
rows.anchor: “Şühedâ”, “şehîd”in cem‘idir. “Şehîd” ise, hâzır, şâhid, nâsır, nümûne-i imtisâl mânalarına gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the challengers are right that their doubt is justified, they should be able to produce an equivalent; ordinary human work normally has a counterpart, as even philosophers say nature is uniform.
rows.anchor: Bir insanın kendiliğinden yaptığı bir şeyi veya daha iyisini diğer insanlardan behemehâl bir yapan bulunur, mu‘tad olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cannot meet the challenge at any time through the Resurrection; even if it were possible in principle, God will not enable them to do so.
rows.anchor: Yapmanız mümkin değil ya, mümkin olsa da yapamayacaksınız, Allah yaptırmayacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The failure warning leads to the dreadful Fire, whose fuel is people and stones and which has been prepared for disbelievers.
rows.anchor: bu ateş, bu nâr-ı cahîm, kâfirler için hazırlanmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Certainty rests on direct perception, rational inference, experience, and report; some recognize the Qur’an’s elevated composition directly, while others learn of it from those who do.
rows.anchor: Bedâhet, şuhûd, istidlâl-i aklî, tecribe, haber, bunlar ilmin, yakīnin en mühim vâsıtaları, mi‘yarlarıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation itself cannot be experimentally repeated because it is a unique divine event, but its effects can be tested; the challenge supplies a special measure whose result can be confirmed across generations.
rows.anchor: Gerçi siz vahyi bizzat tecribe edemezsiniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Testing an effect can reveal whether its cause is general or unique, just as people infer the sun from its light; testing all revelations directly would outlast a lifetime.
rows.anchor: Güneşin doğduğunu ziyâsından anlarsınız. Böyle bir tecribe size sebeb-i vâki‘in küllî ve umûmî mi, yoksa münferid ve mümtaz bir şey mi olduğunu anlatır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge leaves opponents free to try and does not restrain them by force; its categorical forecast and ensuing failure make it an unusually decisive proof of revelation’s inimitability.
rows.anchor: Sizi bir mütegallibin kuvve-i cebriyesiyle bağlamıyor, ikinizi bir yere getirmekten men‘etmiyor. Hür, muhtâr, serbest bırakıyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if critics attribute the Qur’an to Muhammad’s uniquely gifted nature, they should trust his testimony: he calls himself God’s servant and Messenger, seeks no worldly dominion, and asks no wage beyond affection for kin.
rows.anchor: kemâl-i tevâzu‘ile “ben Allah’ın bir kulu ve Resûlüyüm” diyor ve sonra kemâl-i yakīn ile وَلَن تَفْعَلُوا۟ diyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person who doubts God should believe on the testimony of such an exceptional mind; a believer has even stronger reason to accept that God sent the revelation to disclose Himself and His commands.
rows.anchor: Eğer Allah’a inanmıyorsanız, O’nda şüpheniz varsa böyle bir aklın şehâdetiyle O’na inanmanız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once rational, experiential, and scientific grounds for doubt fail, continued suspicion can only arise from obstinacy, self-interest, or immorality; unjustified doubters, like outright deniers, are disbelievers without excuse.
rows.anchor: Bunu bilmez, hâlâ şüphe davasından vazgeçmez, hâlâ kuşkulanırsanız buna inadınızdan, ağrâz-ı şahsiyenizden, ahlâksızlığınızdan başka bir sebep kalmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prediction has been vindicated over 1,344 years: despite rivalry, arms, bloodshed, upheaval, and great expense, no refuting answer was produced; opponents resorted to diversion, while divine justice and the Fire remain.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ın işbu وَلَن تَفْعَلُوا۟ ihbârı o günden bugüne kadar bin üç yüz kırk dört senelik bir tecribe ile sıdkını gösteren bir mu‘cize-i ebediyedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says the stones can refer to the idols and structures worshipped, which help kindle the Fire alongside the people who worshipped them.
rows.anchor: heyâkil-i ma‘bûde olduğu beyan buyuruluyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also reads the wording as indicating combustible stones such as coal; waqūd can denote any kindling or fuel, including grass, tinder, rags, and wood.
rows.anchor: “Vekūd”, ateş yakılan kibrit, ot, çöp, çıra, paçavra

rows.speaker: erbâb-ı fen
rows.claim: Elmalılı reports that experts in the sciences identify the combustible stones as coal.
rows.anchor: erbâb-ı fen bunun taş kömürler olduğunu söylüyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s eloquent address shifts focus among a broad audience, particular groups, opponents, allies, and the Prophet’s special servant, moving from a public warning to a more intimate address.
rows.anchor: nihâyet acı bir inzar ile tamam oldu, derken gülüyor, bir hususiyet daha alıyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says these verses contain the sciences of this world and the hereafter, showing life, its course, and its purpose, as well as the value of human creation before God.
rows.anchor: Bu iki âyette bütün dünya ve âhiret ilimleri mündericdir. Hayat, cereyân-ı hayât, gāye-i hayât gösteriliyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses affirm humanity’s right to benefit from the earth and heavens and summarize the signs of creation and the Creator, establishing God’s creative act, mercy, and favor.
rows.anchor: İnsanın arz u semâ hepsinden hakk-ı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage raises the human spirit from the material and perceptible toward the intelligible, and asks how anyone could turn to disbelief and ingratitude in light of these truths.
rows.anchor: ve bu hakāik karşısında küfür ve küfrâna nasıl

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic rhetorical question powerfully condemns and warns against disbelief and ingratitude; Elmalılı praises the address for its eloquence, purity, sublimity, learning, truth, and moral force.
rows.anchor: Küfür ve küfrânı takbih ve insanları ondan tahzir için bu istifhamdaki tesirin şiddeti ne kadar büyüktür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address reaches all people, especially disbelievers, hypocrites, and sinners: how can they be ungrateful through intellectual or practical disbelief, a condition inconceivable for anyone with knowledge or moral sense?
rows.anchor: Ey insanlar, insan adını taşıyanlar ve ‘ale’l-husûs ey kefere, ey münafıkīn, ey feseka! Allah’a nasıl nankörlük eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All people, individually and collectively, were lifeless before receiving life; they had no inherent possession, being first earth and then a drop in their forefather’s loins.
rows.anchor: siz hepiniz, gerek her biriniz, gerek mecmû‘unuz mukaddemâ hep ölü idiniz, emvât hâlinde idiniz, hayatınız yoktu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave people life and made them embodied, living, thinking humans who breathe, eat, reproduce, sense, think, choose, act, and resist external events through bodily and spiritual powers.
rows.anchor: Allah size hayat verdi, teneffüs, tegaddî, tenasül eder, duyar, düşünür, ister, istediği yere gider, istediği işi yapar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life is not a person’s own property: people cannot even change the color of a single hair, and remembering their former and future states shows that their life was given to them.
rows.anchor: bu hayat sizin kendi malınız olmadığını anlarsınız. O hâlde bu hayatı size bahşeden Allah teâlâ’yı nasıl inkâr eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if God did nothing else for people, His ownership of the life He granted would require faith, worship, and not forgetting Him in attachment to life.
rows.anchor: Allah size hiçbir şey yapmamış ve yapmayacak olsa bile hayatınızın mâliki olduğu için sizin O’na iman ve ubûdiyet etmeniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı voices the objection that inevitable death may seem to justify clinging passionately to temporary pleasures, despite its devastation of homes, families, and lives, then calls that a wretched error.
rows.anchor: Mâdem ki öleceğiz ve mâdem ki Allah verdiğini alıyor, o hâlde hayat elimize geçmiş iken iyi kötü mümkin olan ne zevki varsa görelim diyoruz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even on that mistaken premise, people should seek enjoyment lawfully, treat gratitude and sincerity to God as the greatest pleasure, and love and fear Him for their broad benefits in this life.
rows.anchor: hayatın bu zevklerini böyle körü körüne ve çılgıncasına değil, tarîk-i meşrû‘ile istîfâya çalışmak ve Allah teâlâ’ya ihlâs ve şükrânı en büyük bir zevk bilmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will revive people after death and grant another life, at least as excellent as the first; resurrection after death is true.
rows.anchor: O sizi öldürdükten sonra yine diriltir ve diriltecektir. Size evvel verdiği gibi ve hatta ondan daha a‘lâ yine bir hayat verir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeatability visible throughout the universe underlies natural laws, knowledge, and craft: people can plant seeds, cultivate fields, harvest crops, and repeatedly build or use vehicles because things recur.
rows.anchor: Eğer olmasa idi sen kâinatta hiçbir kanun göremezdin, bir yaptığını bir daha yapamazdın, ilimden, sanattan hiçbir hissen olmazdı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans cannot yet produce and restore life because they do not know life’s law or the primordial secrets of matter and spirits, and lack the power to create in its essence.
rows.anchor: henüz kānûn-ı hayâtı bilemediğinden, henüz maddelerin, rûhların esrâr-ı evveliyesine nüfuz edemediğinden, daha esasında yaratmak, halk etmek kudretine bizzat mâlik olamadığındandır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People cannot see original matter or force, only their products, and their knowledge and power correspond to those manifestations; discovering matter’s secrets would not reveal every force, spirit, or angel or confer creative power.
rows.anchor: Sen asl-ı maddeyi, kuvveti göremezsin, gördüğün onların hâsılları, tezahürleridir. İlmin, fehmin, kudretin de bunlarla mütenâsibdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People can only use matter and force as given; through a more particular relation to God they may, by His permission, gain insight into the mystery of life and reviving.
rows.anchor: onları olduğu kadar alıp Hak teâlâ’nın verdiği rûhunla tasarruf edebileceksin ve bizzat Hak teâlâ’ya daha husûsî bir nisbet peyda edebilirsen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inability to understand or create life does not justify denying the life and life-law already present and applied in each person; these necessarily point to a supreme being who makes and knows them.
rows.anchor: ortada mevcud olan hayat ve ihyâyı da inkâr edemezsin ya? Nefsü’l-emrde bir hayatın ve bir hayat kanununun cereyânında şüphe edemezsin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God made and knows life and its law, what died will live again, and only God can accomplish it; He alone knows how and where, while revelation assures its occurrence.
rows.anchor: bu hayatı yapan ve bunun kanununu bilen bir zât-ı a‘lâ vardır. Hayat ve kānûn-ı hayat hak ve onu yapan ve bilen Hak teâlâ’dır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next life may occur on earth, in heaven, in the grave, or at the Resurrection; its conditions exceed present human understanding, and the afterlife is preceded by the interval of barzakh and grave life.
rows.anchor: Dilerse yerde yapar, dilerse göğe çıkarır, dilerse kabirde yapar, dilerse kıyamette; her hâlde bu bizim diğer bir şe’nimiz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı reports two readings of the revival: life in the grave or the resurrection after the Day of Judgment; either way, events continue beyond this life.
rows.anchor: Buradaki ثُمَّ يُحْيِيكُمْ hayat-ı kabir ile de tefsir edilmiştir. Kıyametten sonra neşr ile de tefsir edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People return to God and are judged by the qualities acquired in their first life, passing the balance to receive reward or punishment; the truth of this is expressed in 99:7–8.
rows.anchor: bu ilk hayatta ne haslet iktisab ettinizse ona göre mîzandan geçecek, mükâfat ve mücâzâtına ereceksiniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At that time, the people of Paradise and divine approval will say, “Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds.”
rows.anchor: Ve o zaman ehl-i cennet ve rıdvân اَلْحَمْدُ للهِّ رَبِّ الْعَالَم۪ينَ diyeceklerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı prays that God help everyone pass the stages of the grave and hereafter with ease and grant them complete faith, righteous deeds, and a good end.
rows.anchor: Cenâb-ı Hak cümlemize imdad etsin, bu geçitleri suhûletle, tatlılıkla geçirsin, îmân-ı kâmil, amel-i sâlih ile hüsn-i hâtime nasib etsin
